PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep group rename draft across list rerenders
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

Fixes an issue where the text typed into a custom group's inline rename box in the Sessions list disappeared when the list refreshed while editing.

## Cause

`SessionGroupRenderer` recreated the `InputBox` on every `renderElement` and reset it to the saved group name. Group rows are re-rendered on every list update, so the draft was lost. Session and chat rows already kept their drafts across re-renders.

## Changes

- Extracted `createInlineRenameInputBox` from the session/chat inline rename helper. It restores the draft value, selection, and focus from an `IInlineRenameValueState`. Session/chat behavior is unchanged.
- The group renderer now keeps a per-group rename state that survives re-renders and is cleared on commit, cancel, or when the group stops editing.
- Added a regression test that types a draft, sets a selection, refreshes the list, and checks that the value, selection, and focus are preserved, and that starting a new rename shows the saved name.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --grep "group rename draft"`: fails without the fix (draft resets to `Group`) and passes with it.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessions*.test.js"`: 761 passing.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.

Not manually verified in a running build.

Scenarios.Scenario: A custom session group is being renamed while a sessions-list refresh or model update rerenders the row.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing synchronous list update rebuilds tree children, rerenders the visible group template, clears its element disposables, captures the old input selection/focus, creates one replacement InputBox, and restores its draft and selection. Only the visible editing group participates in the changed work; sticky scrolling can add one second rendered copy.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: List reconstruction still scales with the existing sessions/groups collection, but the diff-specific work scales with rerender count and the effective cardinality of the active editor: one group, or at most its normal row plus sticky-header copy. Each input event also copies the current short group-name string into the single state object.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All changed DOM work is synchronous on the UI thread. Scheduled list updates are already coalesced to the next animation frame; explicit refresh remains immediate. There is no new parallelism, queue, subprocess, or burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The first render initializes a single in-memory draft from the saved group name; warm rerenders reuse it. Selection and focus are captured during deterministic template cleanup. The state is cleared on commit, cancel, or a non-editing render of that group, so retention is bounded to one draft for the renderer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the renderer call path and one-object lifecycle are explicit in the changed helper and SessionGroupRenderer; no changed boundary call is reachable from rerendering.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh prevalence varies with session activity, but the changed per-refresh work is a bounded set of DOM property reads/writes and one InputBox lifecycle that already existed before the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Before the diff every rerender already disposed and recreated/focused/selected the group InputBox. The diff adds only bounded draft/selection/focus bookkeeping and one lightweight input listener, without increasing editor cardinality or introducing layout, IPC, storage, filesystem, database, network, or subprocess work.

Scenarios.Scenario: The user commits, cancels, or restarts a custom-group rename after one or more rerenders.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Commit clears the draft state, invokes the existing commitGroupEdit path, optionally renames the group, and updates the list; cancel clears state and updates the list. Restart initializes from the authoritative saved group name after the prior state was cleared.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the complete existing session-group state with JSON.stringify during rename persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for a commit that changes a non-empty group name; zero for rerenders, cancellation, and unchanged names.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same commit callback called renameGroup and serialized the same state once before this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously on the rename-commit path, not while preserving a draft across rerenders.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store serialized session-group state through the profile-scoped storage service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage-service call per effective rename commit; no call per keystroke or rerender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same profile-storage store occurred once on an effective group rename before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the existing synchronous commit path only.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The commit-side serialization scales with the existing number of groups and memberships, once per changed non-empty committed name. Rerender count and keystroke count do not multiply commits or storage writes. Cancel and restart add no boundary call.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The commit and profile-storage path is synchronous and singular. The diff adds no concurrency, retry, fan-out, or missing coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Draft state is deliberately invalidated on commit/cancel and a subsequent rename starts cold from the saved name. There is no collection cache, negative-cache state, or unbounded key retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: commit/cancel callbacks, state clearing, renameGroup, and save are directly traced; before/after boundary cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The serialized state can grow with a large sessions/groups profile, but this PR neither changes its size materially nor changes persistence frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new draft state does not defer, duplicate, or fan out commits, and both serialization and storage boundaries retain their prior one-per-effective-rename behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: An existing session or chat inline rename editor is rendered or rerendered through the extracted helper.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The session/chat renderers call the extracted helper, which performs the same container clear, InputBox construction, state restore, input listener, focus/selection behavior, and disposal work that was previously inline before installing the unchanged finish listeners.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective changed cardinality is one active session or chat rename editor per renderer state, per rerender. The helper extraction does not add work per non-editing row or increase collection-wide processing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI-thread DOM work only; no new scheduling or concurrency behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing per-item draft state remains the cache, with the same value, selection, focus, and lifecycle semantics. No cache key or invalidation behavior changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the deleted inline operations and added helper call have a direct one-for-one correspondence, including the existing input listener.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact rerender frequency depends on list activity, but the helper preserves the previous operation count and placement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. This is a mechanical extraction for session/chat rename rendering and does not add expensive work, boundary calls, retained state, or hotter-path execution.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across both changed files and all diff pages. Traced active group rerenders, draft lifecycle, session/chat helper extraction, list-update multiplicity, InputBox teardown, and rename persistence. The PR adds only bounded in-memory UI state and lightweight per-editor bookkeeping; existing full-list rendering and one-per-commit profile persistence are not amplified. No valid performance finding and no performance-regression fix record.
